s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic eruptive facial lesion in a patient with hematologic malignancy
salient_findings: Atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells
Identical pathogenic variations in ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes in bone marrow and skin biopsy specimens
key_facts: 63-year-old man
Asymptomatic new-onset facial lesion
Lesion located under the right lower eyelid
Lesion size: 3×2–mm
Lesion description: smooth, red, dome-shaped papule
History of chronic high-grade myelodysplastic syndrome
History of refractory anemia with excess blasts
Skin biopsy showed atypical dermal infiltrate
Cells in infiltrate were positive for CD207/langerin
Cells in infiltrate were negative for myeloperoxidase
BRAF-V600E variant identified through immunohistochemical studies
Prior bone marrow biopsy showed hypercellular bone marrow
Prior bone marrow biopsy showed atypical erythropoiesis
Myeloblasts present in bone marrow biopsy (10% to 15%)
Identical pathogenic variations in ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes in bone marrow and skin biopsy specimens

shortlist.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin biopsy showed atypical dermal infiltrate positive for CD207/langerin

shortlist.label: Myeloid Sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of chronic high-grade myelodysplastic syndrome and refractory anemia with excess blasts

shortlist.label: Leukemia Cutis
shortlist.why_kept: Asymptomatic eruptive facial lesion in a patient with hematologic malignancy

shortlist.label: Blastic Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cell Neoplasm
shortlist.why_kept: Identical pathogenic variations in ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes in bone marrow and skin biopsy specimens

shortlist.label: Myelodysplastic Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of chronic high-grade myelodysplastic syndrome and refractory anemia with excess blasts

raw.rationale: The presence of a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells positive for CD207/langerin and negative for myeloperoxidase, along with the identification of the BRAF-V600E variant, strongly supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Myeloid Sarcoma
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of myelodysplastic syndrome, the specific immunohistochemical profile of the skin lesion does not align with myeloid sarcoma.

rejected.label: Leukemia Cutis
rejected.why: The lack of myeloperoxidase positivity in the skin biopsy specimen makes leukemia cutis less likely.

rejected.label: Blastic Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cell Neoplasm
rejected.why: The positive staining for CD207/langerin and the presence of the BRAF-V600E variant are more characteristic of Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis than Blastic Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cell Neoplasm.

rejected.label: Myelodysplastic Syndrome
rejected.why: Myelodysplastic syndrome is a condition affecting the bone marrow, and while the patient has this condition, the specific skin lesion described is more indicative of a secondary process like Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis.
